bottom_line: Rivaroxaban versus placebo increased clinically significant bleeding in a dose-dependent manner (hazard ratios [HRs] 2.21 [95% CI 1.25–3.91] for 5 mg, 3.35 [2.31–4.87] for 10 mg, 3.60 [2.32–5.58] for 15 mg, and 5.06 [3.45–7.42] for 20 mg doses; p<0.0001).
implications: In this phase II ACS population, rivaroxaban versus placebo was associated with higher clinically significant bleeding with increasing dose (HRs 2.21 to 5.06; p<0.0001), while the primary efficacy composite showed a non-significant trend (HR 0.79, 95% CI 0.60–1.05; p=0.10) and the main secondary composite (death, myocardial infarction, or stroke) was lower with rivaroxaban (HR 0.69, 95% CI 0.50–0.96; p=0.0270); the trial also states it was not powered to obtain a significant effect for efficacy.

major_points.text: Randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled phase II dose-escalation trial in patients stabilised after acute coronary syndrome, stratified by intended antiplatelet regimen.
major_points.quote: In this randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled, phase II, dose-escalation study, 3491 participants were randomised at 297 sites in 27 countries.

major_points.text: Primary safety endpoint was clinically significant bleeding (TIMI major, TIMI minor, or requiring medical attention).
major_points.quote: The primary safety endpoint was clinically signiﬁcant bleeding (TIMI major, TIMI minor, or requiring medical attention)

major_points.text: Primary efficacy endpoint was death, myocardial infarction, stroke, or severe recurrent ischaemia requiring revascularisation during 6 months.
major_points.quote: the primary eﬃcacy endpoint was death, myocardial infarction, stroke, or severe recurrent ischaemia requiring revascularisation during 6 months.

major_points.text: Clinically significant bleeding increased with rivaroxaban versus placebo in a dose-dependent manner.
major_points.quote: The risk of clinically signiﬁcant bleeding with rivaroxaban versus placebo increased in a dose-dependent manner (hazard ratios [HRs] 2·21 [95% CI 1·25–3·91] for 5 mg, 3·35 [2·31–4·87] for 10 mg, 3·60 [2·32–5·58] for 15 mg, and 5·06 [3·45–7·42] for 20 mg doses; p<0·0001).

major_points.text: Primary efficacy endpoint did not reach statistical significance overall for rivaroxaban versus placebo.
major_points.quote: Rates of the primary eﬃcacy endpoint were 5·6% (126/2331) for rivaroxaban versus 7·0% (79/1160) for placebo (HR 0·79 [0·60–1·05], p=0·10).

major_points.text: Main secondary efficacy endpoint (death, myocardial infarction, or stroke) was reduced with rivaroxaban versus placebo.
major_points.quote: Rivaroxaban reduced the main secondary eﬃcacy endpoint of death, myocardial infarction, or stroke compared with placebo (87/2331 [3·9%] vs 62/1160 [5·5%]; HR 0·69, [95% CI 0·50–0·96], p=0·0270).
